scenes.line1: Can you spot silent data errors?
scenes.say: Can you spot silent errors in your data before they cause trouble? How do you catch them?

scenes.label: Distributions
scenes.sub: Track mean, median, min, max, and histograms to catch outliers.
scenes.say: Distribution monitoring means tracking stats like mean, median, min, max, and histograms to catch outliers or shifts.
Why does this matter? It catches silent errors like data skew, flags anomalies such as sudden mean spikes, and finds issues that basic tests miss.

scenes.title: Detecting a Spike
scenes.say: For example, if the mean of order amount jumps from fifty to five thousand, your alert fires. The histogram shape changes too.

scenes.question: Is basic null-checking enough?
scenes.right: No, distribution shifts can slip past basic checks.
scenes.say: Is basic null-checking enough? No way. Distribution shifts can slip right past simple checks.
